Done. The full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`).

## What I changed

The owner create and update pipelines both normalize email through one shared helper, `OwnerEmail.normalize`, and an invalid email already maps to a 400 via the existing `InvalidEmailException` → `InvalidEmailExceptionHandler`. So the blocklist check belongs in that one place rather than a new pipeline step.

In `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/OwnerEmail.java`:
- Added a `DISPOSABLE_DOMAINS` set (`mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`).
- After the syntactic check, it extracts the (lower-cased) domain and throws `InvalidEmailException` when it's on the blocklist — yielding a 400.

The check runs on the already-normalized (trimmed, lower-cased) value, so casing/whitespace variations like `X@Mailinator.com` are caught too. Because it lives in the shared helper, both `POST /api/owners` and `PUT /api/owners/{ownerId}` reject disposable domains.

The new `AcceptanceTest.errorRejectsDisposableDomain` passes, and the rest of the suite still passes.
